Interacting with Reality

What can a person do once objects, places and people have a digital counterpart?
An HCI-first research atlas: interaction techniques and systems, not a catalogue of computer-vision models.

Four interaction questions

01 · Make objects actionable

How do we select, query, connect and control things?

02 · Capture & remix reality

What can change after the scene becomes editable?

03 · Create in context

How do people sketch, scan, reuse and generate 3D content?

04 · Share people & action

How do capture, placement and awareness change collaboration?

A short historical thread

1968 · Head-tracked display

Make virtual geometry stay put while the viewer moves.

1995 · NaviCam

Recognize the situation and reveal information through a camera.

1997–1999 · Tangible Bits / Urp

Couple physical objects and computational feedback.

1999 · Teddy

Turn drawing into a direct way to construct 3D form.

Compare the human control point

A detector can tell us where an object is. HCI asks what people should be able to do through it. Compare input → representation → human control → outcome. A scan, a live reconstruction, an IoT-state twin and a generated scene are not interchangeable.
